checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar return subnet IDs strictly within [0, 128) for all column_index inputs including edge cases?

reachability.notes: Guaranteed by modular arithmetic for valid inputs, but edge cases with very large or negative column_index could produce unexpected results depending on integer type.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar function implementation. 2. Identify the integer type used for column_index parameter (signed vs unsigned, bit width). 3. Test valid boundary conditions: column_index = 0, column_index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS - 1. 4. Test integer edge cases: column_index at maximum value for the type (e.g., UINT64_MAX, INT64_MAX). 5. Test negative values if signed integer type is used (e.g., -1, INT64_MIN). 6. Verify modular arithmetic implementation cannot produce subnet_id >= 128 or subnet_id < 0 regardless of input. 7. Check for integer overflow/underflow in the calculation path. 8. Validate that DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT equals 128 and is used correctly. 9. Confirm return type cannot represent values outside [0, 128).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0022, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-005:INV-002, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Attacker-controlled input via P2P layer. The property notes edge cases with very large or negative column_index values may bypass expected modular arithmetic guarantees depending on integer type handling. Bug bounty eligible: demonstrate edge-case column_index values producing invalid subnet IDs.

checklist.title: Verify Beacon Node Subnet Routing: Are messages correctly rejected or handled when compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar produces unexpected results from edge-case inputs?

reachability.notes: Guaranteed by modular arithmetic for valid inputs, but edge cases with very large or negative column_index could produce unexpected results depending on integer type.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the data flow from P2P gossip message receipt through to compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar invocation. 2. Identify all validation layers the column_index passes through before reaching the subnet calculation. 3. Verify column_index is validated to be within [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS) BEFORE subnet calculation occurs. 4. Test if malformed gossip messages with out-of-range column_index values are properly rejected at the validation layer. 5. Test what happens if validation is bypassed and an invalid column_index reaches the subnet calculation. 6. Verify error handling when subnet calculation could produce unexpected results. 7. Check for subscription failures or routing errors when invalid subnet IDs might be generated. 8. Confirm the beacon node does not crash or enter an invalid state from edge-case inputs.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0022, Supporting check for actor-beacon-node. Out-of-range subnet IDs could cause subscription failures or messages being published to non-existent subnets, potentially disrupting P2P network operations. Severity justification from property: subscription failures or messages being published to non-existent subnets.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are ALL 13 REJECT validation checks enforced before forwarding data column sidecars to gossip subscribers?

reachability.notes: This is the meta-property ensuring the entire 13-check validation pipeline is correctly ordered and complete. Any check bypass allows malicious sidecars to propagate.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the gossip validation handler for data_column_sidecar topic (SG-006). 2. Map all 13 REJECT-condition checks in the validation pipeline. 3. Verify that validation logic short-circuits on ANY failed check (no early forwarding). 4. Trace message flow to confirm forwarding only occurs AFTER all checks pass. 5. For each REJECT check, craft a malicious sidecar that should fail ONLY that check and verify it is NOT forwarded. 6. Test race conditions: verify no message is forwarded during partial validation. 7. Check for any code paths that bypass the validation pipeline entirely.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0023, Invariant: p2p:SG-006:INV-001, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Critical meta-property for gossip validation - bypassing ANY check allows malicious sidecar propagation. PoC: demonstrate a crafted sidecar that bypasses one or more REJECT checks and gets forwarded.

checklist.title: Verify Subscriber Isolation: Can a malicious P2P peer cause invalid sidecars to reach beacon node or gossip subscribers?

reachability.notes: This is the meta-property ensuring the entire 13-check validation pipeline is correctly ordered and complete. Any check bypass allows malicious sidecars to propagate.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all subscribers to the data_column_sidecar gossip topic (actor-beacon-node, actor-gossip-subscriber). 2. Trace message delivery path from P2P layer to each subscriber. 3. Verify validation occurs BEFORE message delivery to ANY subscriber. 4. Check for any direct message delivery paths that bypass validation. 5. Test with malformed sidecars and verify subscribers never receive them. 6. Verify error cases in validation do not leak partial data to subscribers.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0023, Covers nodes: actor-p2p-peer, actor-beacon-node, actor-gossip-subscriber. Ensures untrusted P2P data cannot reach internal components without validation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are IGNORE conditions in gossip validation properly queuing messages for re-processing without permanent discard or forwarding?

reachability.notes: An attacker can flood IGNORE-path messages (future slots, unseen parents) to exhaust the re-validation queue. Implementations must bound this queue.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the gossip validation pipeline handling data_column_sidecar messages at trust boundary tb-001. 2. Trace all code paths that return IGNORE status. 3. Verify that IGNORE messages are placed into a bounded re-validation queue (not discarded). 4. Confirm IGNORE messages are NOT forwarded to other peers. 5. Test queue behavior under load: flood the node with sidecars referencing unseen parent blocks and verify the queue has proper bounds to prevent memory exhaustion. 6. Verify re-validation triggers correctly when blocking conditions (e.g., parent block arrival) resolve. 7. Check for proper cleanup of stale queued messages to prevent indefinite memory growth.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-006:INV-002, Threat: stride-026. PoC: flood node with sidecars referencing unseen parent blocks, exhausting the IGNORE re-validation queue.

checklist.title: Verify IGNORE Queue Bounds: Is the re-validation queue for IGNORE messages properly bounded to prevent memory exhaustion DoS?

reachability.notes: An attacker can flood IGNORE-path messages (future slots, unseen parents) to exhaust the re-validation queue. Implementations must bound this queue.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the implementation of the IGNORE re-validation queue for data_column_sidecar gossip. 2. Verify the queue has an explicit maximum size limit. 3. Test eviction policy when queue is full (e.g., drop oldest, drop by priority, reject new). 4. Measure memory consumption under sustained IGNORE message flood. 5. Verify rate limiting or backpressure mechanisms exist for IGNORE-inducing messages. 6. Check that legitimate messages are not starved when queue is under attack.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Supporting check for queue bounds. Severity justification: Unbounded IGNORE queue allows memory exhaustion DoS.

checklist.title: Verify IGNORE Message Re-validation: Are queued IGNORE messages correctly re-validated when blocking conditions resolve?

reachability.notes: An attacker can flood IGNORE-path messages (future slots, unseen parents) to exhaust the re-validation queue. Implementations must bound this queue.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the trigger mechanism for re-validating queued IGNORE messages. 2. Create a test scenario: send a data_column_sidecar with an unseen parent block. 3. Verify the message is queued (not discarded). 4. Then provide the missing parent block. 5. Verify the queued sidecar is re-validated and processed correctly. 6. Check for edge cases: reorgs causing parents to become unavailable again, multiple sidecars waiting for same parent. 7. Verify no legitimate sidecars are lost during reorg scenarios.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Covers internal node behavior (actor-beacon-node, actor-p2p-peer). If IGNORE messages are accidentally discarded instead of queued, legitimate sidecars may be lost during reorgs.
